output.answer: As of the latest amendment filed November 10, 2026, Anthropic is positioning a proposed Nasdaq IPO under “ANT” at an estimated $70–$78 per share, with 801,351,354 shares sold by Anthropic and 23,648,646 by selling stockholders. The filing shows extraordinary growth—$33.2 billion of revenue in the nine months ended September 30, 2026, versus $2.5 billion a year earlier—but still a $1.3 billion operating loss and a $104.0 billion net loss for that period. Claude has substantial enterprise traction (more than 11,900 customers generating at least $100,000 of trailing-twelve-month revenue, approximately 900% net revenue retention, and roughly $81 billion of run-rate revenue as of October 31), but that growth comes with extreme compute commitments of approximately $900.9 billion. The other defining takeaway is structural: Anthropic is a public-benefit corporation whose Long-Term Benefit Trust can elect and remove a majority of directors, explicitly prioritizing AI safety alongside shareholder returns.
caveats: The S-1/A-2 is preliminary and not yet effective; the offering size, price, timing, and final terms may change, and the registration statement says the securities may not be sold until it becomes effective.

The $81 billion run-rate revenue figure is an annualized operating metric, not reported period revenue; approximately 900% net revenue retention and the customer-tier counts are company-defined metrics.

The reported net loss includes large changes in the fair value of convertible notes, derivative liabilities, and SAFEs, so it is not the same as the operating loss; the filing also warns that recent revenue growth may not be sustainable.

passages.quote: It is currently estimated that the initial public offering price per share will be between $70.00 and $78.00. We have applied to list our Class A common stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol “ANT.”

Our revenue was $33.2 billion for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, up from $2.5 billion for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. Our operating loss was $1.3 billion for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, down from $5.2 billion for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.
The value that Claude delivers to customers has helped drive our Net Revenue Retention of approximately 900% as of September 30, 2026.

we have entered into purchase commitments and lease agreements ... with an aggregate committed spend of approximately $900.9 billion, substantially all of which is related to compute and infrastructure.

Through a special class of common stock, Class T common stock, the LTBT generally has the authority to elect and remove the Class T directors, who together will constitute a majority of the authorized members of our board of directors.

output.question: What are the key takeaways from Anthropic's S-1 filing?

key_facts.fact: The November 10, 2026 S-1/A-2 estimates an IPO price of $70.00–$78.00 per share, proposes Nasdaq listing under “ANT,” and covers 825,000,000 shares: 801,351,354 sold by Anthropic and 23,648,646 sold by selling stockholders.

Revenue was $33.2 billion for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, versus $2.5 billion for the comparable 2025 period; operating loss was $1.3 billion and net loss was $104.0 billion for the nine months ended September 30, 2026.

As of September 30, 2026, Anthropic reported more than 11,900 customers with at least $100,000 of trailing-twelve-month revenue, more than 1,900 with at least $1 million, and approximately 250 with at least $10 million; it reported approximately 900% net revenue retention and approximately $81 billion of run-rate revenue as of October 31, 2026.

Anthropic reported approximately $900.9 billion of aggregate compute- and infrastructure-related purchase commitments and leases, including approximately $70.7 billion due in the 12 months following September 30, 2026.

Anthropic is a Delaware public-benefit corporation, and its Long-Term Benefit Trust generally has authority through Class T common stock to elect and remove directors who will constitute a majority of the authorized board.

input: What are the key takeaways from Anthropic's S-1 filing?
